speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of a 31-week premature infant with chorioamnionitis, low Apgar scores, and new-onset seizures strongly suggests neonatal sepsis or meningitis. Given the history of maternal infection and the neurological presentation, I suspect an intracranial complication.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Sepsis with Meningitis (likely due to Group B Strep or E. coli given chorioamnionitis).
